task:
Build "Nested and named support groups", step AC-4 of 6: nested, named and editable groups in the web outline, for The Discussion (plan id: nested-named-groups; acceptance criterion: AC-4; source requirements: docs/core-requirements.md; plan base commit 7644616031f5e30bed3392d7f876fcb400537d07). This task text is self-contained: everything needed to implement and verify this step is below.

## Goal

The plan's goal (verbatim):

Support groups can contain sub-groups, and a supporting statement can have its own support groups
as sub-arguments. Status propagates up the tree. Every new group has a required name, and a group's
name and type can be edited.

This task delivers only AC-4, the web front end:
- nested groups are indented under their parent group or supporting statement;
- group rows show their type label, name and holds marker;
- unnamed migrated groups show "Unnamed group" with an "Add a name" control;
- the add form can create a named group under the thesis, a group or a supporting statement;
- group rows can edit a group's name and type.

- Plan: `.zeroshot/plans/nested-named-groups.md` (plan id `nested-named-groups`, `depends_on: [discussion-crud-and-tags]`, source `docs/core-requirements.md`). Test design: `docs/test-plans/nested-named-groups-use-cases.md` (use cases UC-1 to UC-6 with flowcharts, clusters A to C with variables tables, open questions Q-1 to Q-4). The test conditions you need are copied into this task, so the task stands on its own even if that doc is missing from your checkout. Read both files if they are present, but do not modify, move or delete either one. The use-case doc may be an untracked file in the workspace; leave it exactly where it is.

Storage interface: `src/TheDiscussion.Core/Storage/IDiscussionStore.cs`.
- Status: `src/TheDiscussion.Core/Status/ArgumentStatusEngine.cs`. Before this plan it walks only the groups directly under the thesis and their supporting statements, and computes refutation iteratively with an explicit stack so deep chains can't overflow.
- Storage providers: `src/TheDiscussion.Storage.InMemory/InMemoryDiscussionStore.cs` and `src/TheDiscussion.Storage.Postgres/` (EF Core: `DiscussionDbContext.cs`, `Entities.cs`, `PostgresDiscussionStore.cs`, migrations under `Migrations/`: `20261103235923_InitialSchema`, `20261104042910_StatementEditsAndSubtreeDelete`, `20261104043745_MultipleTopicTags`, plus `DiscussionDbContextModelSnapshot.cs`).
- API: `src/TheDiscussion.Api/Discussions/DiscussionEndpoints.cs` and `DiscussionContracts.cs`. The add-statement body is `AddStatementRequest(kind, parentId, text, groupType)`. `StatementResponse` carries the computed `stands` (supporting statements), `refuted` (counter arguments and rebuttals) and `holds` (non-empty groups only; empty groups have no `holds`), plus `editedAt` (always present, `null` until the first edit). Endpoints, all under `/api/v1/discussions`:
  - `POST /{id}/statements` adds a statement (201 with a `StatementResponse`).
  - `PATCH /{id}/statements/{statementId}` edits a statement (200). Before this plan it accepts only `text` and rejects `kind`, `parentId` and `groupType`.
  - `DELETE /{id}/statements/{statementId}` deletes the statement and its whole subtree (204). Deleting the thesis returns 400 naming `statementId`.
  - `GET /{id}` returns the discussion with a flat list of statements in creation order, each with its `parentId`. Status is recomputed on every read and never stored.
- Errors: RFC 7807 `ValidationProblem` with status 400, and an `errors` object keyed by the camelCase field name (`parentId`, `name`, `groupType`, `text`, `kind`, `statementId`, `body`). An unknown discussion or statement returns 404 problem details.
- Wire names. Kinds: `thesis`, `supportGroup`, `supportingStatement`, `illustration`, `counterArgument`, `rebuttal`. Group types: `allRequired` and `anySufficient`, shown in the UI as `ALL REQUIRED` and `ANY SUFFICIENT`. Thesis status: `unsupported`, `open`, `countered`, `tested`.
- Web front end (`web/src/`): `components/Outline.tsx` renders the outline with a recursive `OutlineItem`. Before this plan, group rows show `Support group: <type>` and a `holds` / `does not hold` / `empty` marker, and they have no Edit control. `outline/outline.ts` has `buildOutline`, `groupTypeLabels`, `allowedParentKinds`, `markerFor` and `countBeneath`. `components/AddStatementPanel.tsx` has the "Add support group" form (a target picker and a group type, no name). Other files: `components/Field.tsx`, `api/client.ts`, `api/types.ts`. Web tests use Vitest + React Testing Library with `test/fakeApi.ts` (`mockApi`, `validationProblem`, `networkFailure`, `notFoundProblem`, `referenceDiscussion`), and axe checks live in `test/axe.test.tsx`.
- .NET tests: `tests/TheDiscussion.Core.Tests` (`ArgumentStatusEngineTests.cs`, `TreeBuilder.cs`, `DiscussionRulesTests.cs`, `DiscussionServiceTests.cs`), `tests/TheDiscussion.Api.Tests` (`WebApplicationFactory` tests on the in-memory provider: `ApiFactory.cs`, `DiscussionApiClient.cs`, `DiscussionEndpointTests.cs`, `DiscussionCrudEndpointTests.cs`), `tests/TheDiscussion.Storage.Tests` (`DiscussionStoreContract.cs`, shared by `InMemoryDiscussionStoreContractTests.cs` and `PostgresDiscussionStoreContractTests.cs`, plus `PostgresMigrationsTests.cs` and `PostgresTopicTagsMigrationTests.cs`), and `tests/TheDiscussion.Architecture.Tests` (core and API stay storage-independent).
- PostgreSQL tests run when `THEDISCUSSION_TEST_POSTGRES` holds a connection string. Locally they are skipped with a visible reason when it is unset. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, GitHub Actions with a `postgres:16` service) sets `THEDISCUSSION_REQUIRE_POSTGRES_TESTS=true`, so the PostgreSQL tests are required in CI. Never weaken that.

## Acceptance criterion (verbatim from the plan)

- **AC-4** WHEN a user views a discussion, THE SYSTEM SHALL show nested groups indented under their
  parent group or supporting statement. Each group row shows its type label, its name, and its
  holds or does-not-hold marker. An unnamed migrated group shows "Unnamed group" and an "Add a name"
  control. The add form lets a user add a named group under the thesis, a group or a supporting
  statement. Group rows offer editing of the name and type. API validation errors appear next to
  the field. Check: Vitest + RTL tests with a mocked API, covering rendering three levels of nesting,
  the unnamed state, adding a nested group and editing a group, plus axe checks with no violations.

## Constraints (verbatim from the plan)

- Keep the API conventions (`/api/v1`, camelCase, GUIDs, RFC 7807). The only changes are the new
  `name` field on groups and the new allowed group parents.
- Counter arguments still cannot target groups, and illustrations still cannot be countered.
- No limit on nesting depth. The status engine and every recursive walk (outline rendering,
  cascade delete, serialization) must handle deep trees without recursion that could overflow.
- The schema change ships as an EF Core migration that preserves existing data, and the core and
  API projects stay storage-independent.
- No accounts or authorization; the endpoints are as open as the existing ones.

How they apply to this task: the front end talks to the API only through `web/src/api/client.ts`. Outline building and rendering must handle deep trees without recursion that could overflow.

## Decided approach (verbatim from the plan; the outline reference this task must match)

- Outline reference: the existing outline. It is extended by indenting nested groups and showing
  each group's name after its type label, for example:

```
[THESIS]  Remote work boosts productivity            (TESTED)
  + ALL REQUIRED: Productivity mechanisms             (holds)
  |   [SUPPORT] Fewer interruptions                   (standing)
  |   + ANY SUFFICIENT: Evidence                      (holds)
  |   |   [SUPPORT] Studies show +13% output          (standing)
  |   |   [SUPPORT] Survey of 500 managers            (countered)
  |   |      x [COUNTER] Self-reported data           (unrefuted)
  |   [SUPPORT] No commute saves energy               (standing)
  |      + ALL REQUIRED: Why commuting drains energy  (holds)
  |      |   [SUPPORT] Average commute is 54 minutes  (standing)
  + ANY SUFFICIENT: Unnamed group  [Add a name]       (holds)
  |   ...
```

## Decisions that apply

- **D-1** Groups can nest inside groups and sit under supporting statements as sub-arguments. (Wayne)
- **D-3** Group names are required for new groups, 1 to 100 characters. Existing groups migrate unnamed and show a prompt to add a name. (Wayne)
- **D-4** No fixed nesting-depth limit. (Wayne)
- **D-5** Changing a group's type or name is an edit: it sets `editedAt`, like a text edit. (assumed)

## Implementation notes

- `api/types.ts` and `api/client.ts`:
  - Statements carry `name: string | null`.
  - The add-statement request carries `name` for groups.
  - Add a client call for editing a group that sends `PATCH` with `name` and/or `groupType`, and never `text`.
- `outline/outline.ts`:
  - Set `allowedParentKinds.supportGroup` to the thesis, `supportGroup` and `supportingStatement`.
  - Keep `buildOutline` and `countBeneath` iterative.
  - Group labels follow the reference, for example `ALL REQUIRED: Productivity mechanisms`. An unnamed group reads `ANY SUFFICIENT: Unnamed group` with an `Add a name` control.
- `components/Outline.tsx`:
  - Indent nested groups under their parent group or supporting statement, with each group's marker (`holds`, `does not hold`, or `empty` when `holds` is absent).
  - Show the `(edited)` marker on edited groups.
  - Keep the existing Delete control.
  - Group rows offer Edit for name and type, with no text editing.
  - Each nesting level is a recursive `OutlineItem`. If that can't render the deep-tree test, replace it with an iterative flattening, such as a flat list with a depth level for indentation and accessible structure.
- `components/AddStatementPanel.tsx`: the "Add support group" form offers every valid target (the thesis, every group at any depth and every supporting statement at any depth), a required name field using `Field`, and the group type.
- Errors:
  - API validation errors appear next to their field with `aria-invalid` and a description. The form stays open and keeps the user's input.
  - A failure with no field errors, or a network failure, shows a form-level alert.
- Existing web tests:
  - They must still pass. You may add `name` to fixtures where the types now need it.
  - If an existing test asserts the old `Support group: <type>` label, update only that expected label text to the reference format, and list it in your summary.
  - Do not change any other assertion.

## Testing

Source: `docs/test-plans/nested-named-groups-use-cases.md`:
- UC-4: main flow steps 1 to 7, alternate flows A1 to A3, error flows E1 to E4, and the postconditions. Its decision points are "Group parent kind?", "Group has a name?", "holds present in response?", "User action?" and "API response?".
- The Cluster B variables "UI nesting shown", "`holds` marker shown", "API error field returned to UI", "Add-form target kind", "Migrated null-name group" (UI part), "`name` length after trimming" (only showing the server's 400; the server owns the rule) and "Accessibility checks".

Leave out delete over nested trees (AC-5) and the manual readability review (AC-6).

The plan's check for AC-4 (verbatim): Check: Vitest + RTL tests with a mocked API, covering rendering three levels of nesting,
  the unnamed state, adding a nested group and editing a group, plus axe checks with no violations.

Vitest + React Testing Library tests with the API mocked through `web/src/test/fakeApi.ts`. Add a nested fixture next to `referenceDiscussion()`.
- Three levels of nesting (Cluster B "UI nesting shown", boundary of exactly 3 levels):
  - A group inside a group inside a group, each rendered inside or indented under its parent row. Assert the structure (for example with `within(parentRow)` or nesting level), not only the text.
  - A sub-argument group under a supporting statement, rendered under that support.
- Group rows show the type label (`ALL REQUIRED` and `ANY SUFFICIENT`), the name, and each marker: `holds`, `does not hold`, and `empty` when `holds` is absent (Cluster B "`holds` marker shown").
- Deep trees (Cluster B "UI nesting shown": deep, 100 or more levels):
  - In `outline/outline.test.ts`, `buildOutline` handles a 1,000-level chain.
  - An RTL render of a tree 100 or more levels deep completes without error.
- Unnamed state (UC-4 A1; Cluster B "Migrated null-name group"):
  - A group with `name: null` shows "Unnamed group" and an "Add a name" control.
  - Activating the control opens the edit form with focus on the name field.
  - Saving a valid name sends `PATCH` with `{ name }`. After the reload, the name replaces "Unnamed group".
- Adding a nested group (UC-4 main flow steps 4 and 5; Cluster B "Add-form target kind"):
  - The target options include the thesis, a top-level group, a nested group and a supporting statement, including a nested one.
  - Submitting sends `POST` with `{ kind: "supportGroup", parentId, name, groupType }`.
  - After the reload, the new group appears under the chosen target.
- Editing a group (UC-4 main flow steps 6 and 7):
  - Edit on a group row opens a form with the current name and type.
  - Changing only the name sends `PATCH` with `name`. Changing only the type sends `groupType`. Changing both sends both. No request ever sends `text`.
  - After the reload, the row shows the new values, `(edited)`, and the recomputed markers and thesis status from the mocked response.
  - Group rows offer no text editing.
- Cancel (UC-4 A2): cancelling the add form or the edit form sends no request, and focus returns to the control that opened it.
- Errors (UC-4 E1 to E4; Cluster B "API error field returned to UI"):
  - A 400 naming `name`, for both a whitespace-only name and a 101-character name submitted to the mock, shows the message next to the name field. The field has `aria-invalid="true"`, and the form stays open with the user's input.
  - A 400 naming `parentId`, for a target deleted in the meantime, shows the message next to the target picker.
  - A 400 naming `groupType` shows the message next to the type choice.
  - Several field errors at once each show next to their own field.
  - A network failure (`networkFailure`), and a 400 with no field errors, show a form-level alert.
- Q-1 in the UI: changing only the type of an unnamed group, when the mock returns 400 naming `name`, shows the error next to the name field.
- axe checks (`web/src/test/axe.test.tsx`; Cluster B "Accessibility checks"): no violations on the outline with nested and unnamed groups, the add-group form and the group edit form, each in its normal and its error state.
- All existing web tests still pass.

## Open questions (from the test-plan doc; flag, don't settle silently)

- **Q-1:** AC-3 built the strict reading, in which a `groupType`-only `PATCH` on an unnamed group returns 400 naming `name`. The UI should guide the user to the name field (the "Add a name" control focuses it). Don't work around the rule on the client, for example by sending a made-up name. If the strict reading makes the UI awkward, say so in your summary.
- **Q-4:** the server counts name length in UTF-16 code units. If you add a client-side length hint or `maxLength`, it must count the same way (HTML `maxlength` does) and must never block a name the server would accept. The server's 400 stays the source of truth.
